What is a GPU?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerIntegrated and dedicated graphicsWhy games use a GPUBefore an upgradeFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

A GPU is a processor designed to perform many calculations in parallel. It creates graphics for your screen and can also accelerate suitable computing tasks.

Integrated and dedicated graphics

Integrated graphics share the processor package or system design and commonly use system memory. A dedicated graphics card has its own processor and typically its own video memory. Not every computer needs a separate card.

Why games use a GPU

A game needs to draw many pixels, surfaces, and lighting effects repeatedly. GPUs are designed for this parallel work. Frame rate also depends on the CPU, game engine, settings, and display resolution.

Before an upgrade

Check power requirements, case clearance, motherboard connections, and monitor ports. For laptops, the graphics hardware is usually not replaceable. Compare performance in the actual software you use.
